cards.task: Pick up the key, then reach the goal.

wrong.why: Takes the key and opens the door, then waits and never reaches the goal.
Never takes the key and never reaches the goal.

paraphrases: Take the key and then get to the goal.

cards.notes: The other clause is implied by the finish, so the env reward pays exactly when it is done. Card fixes 2026-11-18: Existence(at_goal) alone is also correct, because reaching the goal already needs the key; the no-goal cards of the template isolate the clause. Chain prompt loop 2026-11-19: the task states an order, so the primary answer is the chain form (Existence of the last step plus Precedence). The order is forced, so the Precedence is optional and Existence(at_goal) alone still matches `expect`. One Existence per step, alone or with the Precedence, is `also_ok` because the level forces the order, and the judge stays lenient on purpose; the critic rejects an Existence that the chain already forces, so it rejects these answers on purpose. The prompts still write every order the task states, forced or not; only this card is lenient about a forced Precedence. The idle walk breaks only clause 1 (`breaks: [1]`): clause 0 is now the Precedence, which a run that never takes the key keeps.

cards.task: Whenever you are holding the key, the door must be open at that moment or opened afterwards. Pick up the key, open the door with it, then pick up the box in the other room.

wrong.why: Takes the key, then waits: the door is never opened.
Takes the key and opens the door, then waits and never picks up the box.

paraphrases: At any moment you are holding the key, the door has to be open then or opened later. Take the key, open the door with it and then take the box in the other room.
If you are holding the key, the door must be open at that point or at a later point. Pick up the key, use it to open the door, and then pick up the box in the other room.
Any time the key is in your hands, the door must be open right then or opened afterwards. Take the key and open the door with it. Finally, pick up the box in the other room.
cards.notes: Moved from KeyCorridorS6R3 to UnlockPickup on 2026-11-20: no method (no-RM, ARM-FM, FARM) learned KeyCorridor in 71 runs, so the card could not train, and UnlockPickup was learned (ARM-FM 3 of 3, FARM 1 of 3 on base-unlock-pickup at 1.5M steps). The trigger is has_door_key, a condition that stays true while the key is held, so the door must be open when the key was last held or later (the wording of tpl-response-2-goal and -3-goal); the old key_found trigger and its last-step reading went with the level. The goal forces the door open, so the Response only separates a run that takes the key and stops; a wait plan fails the goal. Chain reword 2026-11-19, kept: the task names every step, so the answer is the chain Existence(box), Precedence(door_open, box), Precedence(has_door_key, door_open) plus the card's Response. Both orders are forced by the level (`forced`: the door opens only with the matching key, the box room has no other entrance), and the progress pay reads the machine, so a step with no rule of its own would pay nothing.

cards.task: Whenever the ball is out of the way of the door, you must be holding the key at that moment or pick it up afterwards.

wrong.why: Moves the ball, then waits and never takes the key.

paraphrases: At every moment the ball is out of the way of the door, you have to be carrying the key then, or pick it up later.
If the ball has been moved away from the door, you must be holding the key at that point or at some later point.
Any time the ball is away from the door, the key must be in your hands at that moment or afterwards.
cards.notes: Changed in card fix 2: the trigger blocker_moved is a condition, not a latch (false again when the ball is dropped back on its cell), so Response needs the key in hand at the last moment the ball was out of the way or later. The task says exactly that and not 'keep holding it': a run that puts the key down and takes it again, or restores the ball and then takes and drops the key, satisfies the clause.

Card fixes 2026-11-18: a wait plan passes it on seeds 1-3 (the exit is never reached), so it no longer trains (train false); the same Precedence gate, with its trigger forced by a goal, is tested where waiting fails by tpl-precedence-1-goal. S2 2026-11-19: RespondedExistence(at_exit, switch_toggled) is also a correct output (`also_ok`): at_exit holds only on the last step and never together with switch_toggled, so a toggle can only come before it and the two readings accept and reject the same runs; the goal twin that trains is tpl-precedence-4-goal.
